cases.request: Develop this premise into a feature story bible, character arcs, and sequence outline: a paramedic begins receiving emergency calls from tomorrow.
expect: Stress-tests whether the premise can sustain feature-length choices, escalation, and consequences
Builds a coherent story bible without forcing one named beat-sheet formula
Defines character wants, pressures, relationships, arc possibilities, world rules, setups, and payoffs
Produces a causal sequence outline that includes the ending or clearly labels it as open

cases.request: Turn these notes into a nonlinear ensemble feature. Keep the same six characters and final event, but solve the chronology and make every storyline affect the others.
expect: Preserves the six characters and locked ending
Designs legible causal and information flow without forcing a conventional linear structure
Tracks what each character and the audience know across chronology shifts
Makes the storylines collide through choices and consequences rather than thematic resemblance alone

cases.request: Write the opening ten screenplay pages from this approved outline. Preserve the cold open, the protagonist's existing voice, and the reveal on page ten.
expect: Reads the outline and any existing voice evidence before drafting
Writes screenplay pages rather than a prose synopsis
Preserves the cold open and reveal while building causal scene pressure
Uses readable screenplay form and avoids unnecessary camera or acting direction

cases.request: Continue my feature through sequence four using the canonical Fountain draft, story bible, and continuity ledger in this project. Update the files but do not change locked dialogue.
expect: Locates and reads the canonical project artifacts before writing
Uses file tools only when available and authorized, without creating duplicate canonical drafts
Drafts a coherent connected unit and preserves locked dialogue
Updates continuity and revision state and reports exactly what was completed

cases.request: Write the entire feature screenplay from this treatment, but I do not have file tools connected in this chat.
expect: Continues with screenplay work that can be done in conversation
Plans coherent drafting units and maintains a compact story and continuity state
States the exact portion delivered rather than claiming a truncated response is a complete feature
Offers an export-ready or manual persistence path without requiring a connector

cases.request: Fix the slow second act without changing the ending, the sister's betrayal, or the observatory location. Diagnose it first, then rewrite only what needs to change.
expect: Diagnoses upstream causes using evidence from the supplied material
Treats the ending, betrayal, and observatory as locked
Builds a revision map that tracks affected setups, payoffs, and continuity
Rewrites the smallest coherent units that can materially solve the pacing problem

cases.request: Polish the dialogue in scenes 18 through 21. Keep every plot fact and make Lena and Omar sound less interchangeable without writing accents phonetically.
expect: Preserves every plot fact and surrounding story state
Differentiates voice through worldview, strategy, vocabulary, syntax, and silence
Avoids phonetic caricature and excessive parentheticals
Checks that exposition and information ownership remain correct

cases.request: Give me full coverage on this screenplay. Cite scenes and prioritize the three highest-leverage changes, but do not rewrite anything.
expect: Reviews the available screenplay rather than relying on the author's explanation
Supports strengths and concerns with scene, beat, page, or passage evidence
Prioritizes recommendations by leverage and dependency
Does not rewrite screenplay pages

cases.request: Compare drafts three and four and tell me whether the protagonist became more active. Track regressions as well as improvements.
expect: Aligns corresponding scenes despite numbering or ordering changes
Evaluates protagonist agency using choices and consequences in the actual pages
Reports improvements, regressions, and new continuity obligations
Does not assume the newer draft is better

cases.request: Prepare scenes 62 through 66 for visual development, acting direction, and video production without changing the screenplay.
expect: Creates standalone scene intent sheets grounded in the canonical screenplay
Exports story state, objectives, hidden information, required action, exact dialogue, and continuity
Keeps narrative requirements separate from visual design, acting micro-behavior, camera, and model syntax
Labels locked, provisional, and open fields where ambiguity could cause drift

cases.request: I want to keep the screenplay in my Claude project and send approved drafts to a connected production service. Show me how this skill handles connectors before writing anything.
expect: Explains that the skill and the connector are separate capabilities
Checks the active surface and already available tools before recommending setup
Provides Claude-appropriate remote connector or Claude Code MCP guidance
Covers authentication, least permissions, verification, external-write approval, and manual fallback without beginning screenplay work

cases.request: Draft this sequence using the writing model connected to this chat, and save the result to the existing screenplay file.
expect: Inspects the connected tool and its actual model, input, output, and write capabilities
Uses the user-selected external model rather than substituting a hardcoded provider
Preserves the canonical screenplay and obtains any required write approval
Verifies the returned text and saved destination before claiming completion
Explains long-form screenplay development, drafting, revision, coverage, and production handoff without working on a screenplay
Lists develop, draft, revise, coverage, and help modes
Provides a starter and another realistic example for every mode
Explains conversation, persistent-project, connected-workflow, and manual-handoff choices plus connector setup boundaries

expect: Does not invoke the feature-screenwriting workflow merely to create a video-generation prompt

cases.request: Generate a four-view character design sheet and five facial expressions from this visual reference.
